title: Chaku: What It Is, and How to Make It at Home
seoTitle: Chaku for Maghe Sankranti: What It Is and How to Make It
description: Chaku is the dark jaggery sweet Nepal eats at Maghe Sankranti. What it is, why Tokha makes it, and a 50-minute recipe for 20 to 25 pieces that sets.
content:
In Tokha in the middle of January the lanes smell of hot ghee and jaggery from early morning, and there are men working a rope of dark sugar back and forth on a hook until it turns the colour of old brass. Most of the country buys chaku. Tokha makes it.

You can also make it at home, on a normal stove, and it is easier than it looks in exactly one respect and harder in exactly one other.

We should say at the start that we do not sell chaku (चाकु). We make the sakhar (सख्खर), or jaggery, that chaku is made from, in the hills of Sankhuwasabha. So this is a recipe, not a product page with a recipe attached, and we have written it the way we would explain it to a neighbour.

> Chaku (चाकु) is a dark, chewy Nepali sweet made from jaggery, ghee and sesame, eaten at Maghe Sankranti in January. You melt the jaggery, reduce it to the thread stage, then work it off the heat until it thickens and pales. That thread stage decides everything: too far and it sets rock hard, too early and it never sets.

## Ingredients

- 500 g sakhar block, broken into small pieces
- 3 tablespoons ghee, plus a little more for the tray and your hands
- 100 g white sesame seeds (til)
- 2 tablespoons water
- 50 g roasted peanuts or almonds, roughly chopped (optional)

A word on which jaggery to use, because it matters more than any other choice here. A hard, well-reduced [sakhar block](/products/organic-jaggery-block) is what you want. It carries less moisture than a soft block, so it reaches the thread stage predictably and sets firm without going sticky in a warm kitchen.

[Sakhar powder](/products/jaggery-powder) will work, and it melts faster, which is a genuine advantage if you are nervous. It also catches and scorches faster for the same reason, so keep the heat lower and stir from the first minute. We have not run the two side by side in a controlled way, so treat that as a cook's opinion rather than a tested result.

Avoid a very soft, wet block. That is where most chaku that refuses to set comes from.

## Equipment

Use a heavy pan. Iron, a thick-based kadhai or copper if you have it.

This is not fussiness. Sugar at the thread stage is above the temperature at which it starts to burn, and a thin pan puts all of that heat straight into the layer touching the metal. In a thin pan you get scorched, bitter chaku while the middle is still not ready, and there is no way to rescue it.

You also want a bowl of cold water beside the stove, a greased tray or thali, and a wooden or steel spatula you do not mind working hard.

## Method

### Step 1: Roast the til and set it aside

Dry roast the sesame seeds in the pan over a low flame, moving them constantly, until they turn a shade darker and start to pop and smell nutty. This takes a few minutes.

Tip them straight out onto a plate. Sesame keeps cooking in a hot pan and goes bitter quickly. Do this first, while the pan is clean, and get it out of the way.

### Step 2: Melt the sakhar with ghee and water

Put the broken sakhar, the ghee and the 2 tablespoons of water into the heavy pan over a low to medium flame.

The water is not part of the recipe so much as insurance. It gives the jaggery time to melt evenly before anything gets hot enough to catch. Stir steadily. Do not walk away, and do not raise the heat to speed it up.

You are done with this stage when there are no lumps left and the mixture is smooth and glossy.

### Step 3: Reduce it to the thread stage

Now keep it at a steady simmer and stir. It will foam up, then settle, then start to thicken and darken. Depending on your pan and flame this takes somewhere around 10 to 20 minutes.

This is the stage that decides the batch, so test it rather than trusting the clock. Drop a little of the syrup into your bowl of cold water. What you are looking for:

:::table Reading the cold water test when making chaku
What happens in the water | What it means | What to do
It disperses and clouds the water | Not ready. Nowhere near | Keep going
It sinks and forms a soft thread you can lift | Thread stage. This is chaku | Take it off the heat now
It forms a soft ball you can squash | Slightly past. Still workable | Off the heat immediately, work fast
It forms a hard ball or snaps | Too far. It will set like glass | Stop. See the rescue note below
:::

If you prefer a cue you can see rather than feel, lift the spatula and let the syrup fall. At the thread stage it stops pouring in a sheet and starts falling in a single slow strand.

Trust the water test over both. It is the one that has been used for this since long before thermometers.

### Step 4: Work it off the heat

Take the pan off the flame and keep stirring, hard, in one direction.

This is the part nobody tells you about and it is where real chaku comes from. As it cools it will start to resist the spoon, lose its shine, and lift from a translucent dark brown towards an opaque, lighter, brassy colour. That colour change is air going in.

Two to five minutes of honest work. If your arm is not tired you probably have not done it.

The artisan version in Tokha goes much further than this, pulling the mass over a hook again and again until it is genuinely pale and layered. You cannot really do that in a home kitchen and you do not need to.

### Step 5: Fold in the til

Add the roasted sesame, and the nuts if you are using them, and fold them through quickly and evenly.

Work fast here. The mixture is stiffening every second, and once it stops moving you cannot distribute anything through it.

### Step 6: Set and cut

Tip it onto the greased tray and flatten it with a greased spatula or the back of a greased steel bowl. Aim for about a centimetre thick.

Score it into pieces while it is still warm, using a greased knife. Do not wait until it is cold and then try to cut it, because cold chaku shatters along its own lines rather than yours.

Leave it to set completely at room temperature, which takes an hour or two, then break along the score lines.

![Finished til chaku cut into pieces, made at home with sakhar jaggery for Maghe Sankranti](/blog/chaku-recipe-maghe-sankranti/chaku-recipe-maghe-sankranti-nepal.jpg "This is what you are aiming for: matte, not glassy, and it snaps rather than bends.")

## Why Chaku Fails, and What to Do

Four failures cover almost every batch that goes wrong.

**It burned and tastes bitter.** The heat was too high or the pan was too thin. There is no fix once it has caught; the bitterness goes all the way through. Start again with a heavier pan and a lower flame.

**It will not set.** You stopped before the thread stage, or the jaggery was a soft, wet block carrying too much moisture. If it is still in the pan, put it back on a low flame and reduce further, testing in cold water every minute or two.

**It set rock hard.** You went past the thread stage into hard ball. It is edible, it is just brutal. Break it small and eat it as a hard sweet, and next time take the pan off earlier than feels right.

**It is grainy.** Usually undissolved jaggery from step 2, or it was stirred while it was cooling in a way that started crystallisation. Make sure the melt is completely smooth before you let it climb in temperature.

## Varieties of Chaku

The base is always jaggery and ghee. What goes into it is regional and personal.

- **Til chaku** is the classic and the one most associated with Maghe Sankranti. Sesame, nothing else.
- **Badam chaku** uses roasted peanuts, whole or crushed.
- **Nariwal chaku** folds in dried coconut.
- **Khuwa chaku** adds reduced milk solids, which makes it softer and richer and shortens how long it keeps.

The method is the same for all of them. Only the fold at step 5 changes.

Chaku is also the filling in [yomari](/blog/yomari-chaku-recipe), the steamed rice-flour dumplings Newar families make at Yomari Punhi, about a month before Maghe Sankranti. There it is kept softer, so it runs when the yomari is broken open.

## Why Nepal Eats Chaku at Maghe Sankranti

Maghe Sankranti falls in mid-January and marks the sun beginning its northward journey. It is the turn of the winter, and the food is chosen for it: chaku, til, ghee, tarul and sweet potato, all warm, dense and full of energy for the coldest weeks of the year.

There is a straightforward logic in that. These are the things a hill household had in January, and they are the things worth eating when it is cold.

Tokha, north of Kathmandu, is the historic centre of the trade. [All India Radio's Kathmandu report](https://www.newsonair.gov.in/kathmandu-streets-full-oof-fragrance-of-freshly-cookled-jaggery-for-maghe-sankranti) describes the streets filling with the smell of freshly cooked jaggery in the run-up to the festival, which is exactly what it is like. The families there have made it for generations, and the pulled, layered chaku they produce is a different thing from what comes off a home stove. It is worth buying theirs at least once to know what the ceiling looks like.

The ingredient underneath all of it is ordinary unrefined cane sugar, the same [non-centrifugal cane sugar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-centrifugal_cane_sugar) family that panela and gur belong to, and in Nepal that means sakhar or gur.

## How to Store Chaku

Room temperature, in an airtight box, with the pieces in a single layer or separated by paper.

It keeps well for a few weeks. What ends it is humidity, not age: chaku pulls moisture out of the air, goes tacky and then starts to slump. Do not refrigerate it, because taking it in and out puts condensation directly onto the surface, which is worse than leaving it in a cupboard.

If it has gone slightly sticky, it is still fine to eat.

## Where Can You Buy Chaku in Kathmandu?

Not from us. People search for chaku online and land on this page, and we would rather send you to the right place than sell you something close to it.

If you want the real pulled, layered chaku, buy it from Tokha. In the weeks before Maghe Sankranti it is sold in Tokha itself and in markets across the Valley. Buy it from someone who makes it. Good chaku is matte and a lighter, brassy brown, and it snaps cleanly. A very glossy, dark slab is closer to set jaggery than to worked chaku.

We do not quote a chaku price, because we do not sell it and have not checked what makers are charging this season. It varies with the maker, with how much sesame and nut goes in, and with how close to Sankranti you buy. If you want to know what the jaggery inside it costs, [our sakhar price list](/sakhar-price) sets that out.

If you would rather make it, one [1kg sakhar block](/products/organic-jaggery-block) is two batches of the recipe above, which is 40 to 50 pieces.

## Making Chaku in Quantity

Most people reading this are making one batch for the family. If that is you, buy a single block, skip this section and go back to the fire.

Some of you are not. If you are making chaku to sell, the thing that catches people out is not the method, it is the calendar. Mid-January is one date the whole country shares, so the week you think to order is the week everybody else does.

That is why we ask for anything aimed at Maghe Sankranti to be agreed months in advance rather than weeks. Lead time is longer during the crushing season, not shorter, which is the opposite of what most people assume.

What a chaku maker needs from the sakhar is hardness and low moisture. A soft, damp block fights you at the thread stage before you have properly started, and that is a property of how the block was made and how long it has been standing. It is not something you can correct in the kadhai.

If you are buying at that scale, the terms are on our [wholesale page](/wholesale). If you are making a tray or two, one [1kg sakhar block](/products/organic-jaggery-block) is more than enough, and we would rather say so than sell you five.

## The Honest Note About Eating It

Chaku is jaggery, ghee and sesame. It is delicious and it is extremely dense in sugar and fat, which is the entire point of a festival food eaten in the coldest week of the year.

It is not a health food, and the fact that it is made with unrefined jaggery rather than white sugar does not change that in any way that matters. We have set out the whole comparison in [sakhar and sugar, honestly](/blog/jaggery-vs-sugar), and if diabetes is in the room, please read [whether jaggery is safe for diabetics](/blog/is-jaggery-safe-for-diabetics) before the tray goes round.

Eat it at Sankranti. Enjoy it properly. Then put the tray away.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### What is chaku made of?

Chaku is made from jaggery and ghee, cooked down to the thread stage and worked until it thickens, usually with roasted sesame folded through. Peanuts, coconut or khuwa are common variations. There is nothing else in a traditional chaku.

### What is the difference between chaku and sakhar?

Sakhar, or gur, is the raw ingredient: unrefined cane sugar boiled down and set into blocks. Chaku is a finished sweet made from it, by remelting the jaggery with ghee and working it. All chaku starts as sakhar; sakhar is not chaku.

### Which jaggery is best for chaku?

A hard, well-reduced block with low moisture. Soft, wet blocks are the most common reason chaku refuses to set, because the extra water changes how the syrup behaves. Powdered jaggery works and melts faster, but it also scorches faster.

### Why did my chaku not set?

Almost always because it came off the heat before the thread stage. Test in cold water rather than watching the clock: it should sink and form a soft thread you can lift. Very soft or wet jaggery is the other common cause.

### Why do Nepalis eat chaku on Maghe Sankranti?

Maghe Sankranti marks the sun's northward turn in mid-January, and it is celebrated with warm, energy-dense winter foods: chaku, til, ghee, tarul and sweet potato. These are the things a hill household had in the coldest part of the year, and the tradition has held.

### Can chaku be made without ghee?

You can reduce the ghee but not remove it. Ghee stops the sugar from setting into a solid glassy sheet and gives chaku the texture that makes it chaku. Oil is a poor substitute and changes the taste noticeably.

### How long does chaku keep?

A few weeks at room temperature in an airtight box. Humidity is what ends it rather than age, so keep it dry and out of the fridge, where condensation forms on the surface every time you take it out.

### Where can I buy chaku in Kathmandu?

From Tokha, where it is made, or from markets across the Kathmandu Valley in the weeks before Maghe Sankranti. We do not sell chaku. We sell the sakhar it is made from, and the recipe on this page makes 20 to 25 pieces from 500 g.

## One Last Thing

If your first batch sets hard, that is the normal first batch. The thread stage is a feel more than a fact, and nobody gets it from reading about it.

The ingredient is worth getting right, though, because everything in chaku is the jaggery. If you want to know what to look for before you buy any, we have written [how to identify pure sakhar](/blog/how-to-identify-pure-jaggery-sakhar), and [what makes hill sakhar different](/blog/himalayan-jaggery-sankhuwasabha) explains why blocks vary so much between one shop and the next. If you are curious about ours, [this is where it comes from](/our-story).

Make it once before Sankranti so the real batch is your second one.

title: सख्खर खाने फाइदा र यथार्थ
seoTitle: सख्खर खाने फाइदा: साँचो कति, बढाइचढाइ कति
description: सख्खर खाने फाइदा कति साँचो हो र कति बढाइचढाइ, एक सख्खर उत्पादकको इमानदार जवाफ, र दिनमा कति खानु ठीक हो भन्ने WHO को सुझाव।
content:
बिहान चिया पकाउँदै गर्दा हातमा सख्खरको डल्लो हुन्छ, र मनमा एउटा प्रश्न: यो साँच्चै चिनीभन्दा राम्रो हो त?

सख्खर (sakhar, कतै सख्खर त कतै गुड भनिन्छ) खाने फाइदाबारे इन्टरनेटमा लेखिएका कुरा प्रायः एकनासका छन्। रगत सफा गर्छ, कलेजो सफा गर्छ, तौल घटाउँछ। हामी सख्खर बनाएर बेच्ने मान्छे हौं, सङ्खुवासभाको पहाडमा, दाउराको आगोमा कराहीमा उमालेर। त्यही भएर यो लेख अलि फरक हुनेछ।

यहाँ हामी साँचो फाइदा कति हो, बढाइचढाइ कहाँ भएको छ, र एक दिनमा कति खानु ठीक हो भन्ने कुरा सिधा लेख्नेछौं।

> सख्खर चिनीभन्दा थोरै राम्रो हो, तर धेरै राम्रो होइन। यो परिष्कृत नगरिएको हुनाले फलाम, पोटासियम र म्याग्नेसियमजस्ता खनिज अलिकति बाँकी रहन्छन्, र सल्फर वा रङ्ग हालिँदैन। तर यो पनि चिनी नै हो। क्यालोरी उस्तै छ र रगतको चिनी उस्तै बढाउँछ।

## पहिले इमानदार कुरा: सख्खर पनि चिनी नै हो

हामी सख्खर बेच्छौं, र पहिलो कुरा त्यही लेख्दैछौं जसले हाम्रै बिक्री घटाउँछ।

सख्खर भनेको उखुको रस उमालेर पानी उडाएपछि बाँकी रहने चिनी हो। त्यसको ठूलो भाग सुक्रोज हुन्छ, ठ्याक्कै त्यही सुक्रोज जुन सेतो चिनीमा हुन्छ।

शरीरले चिनीलाई परम्परागत हो कि होइन भनेर छुट्याउँदैन। सख्खरले पनि रगतको ग्लुकोज बढाउँछ। सेतो चिनीले पनि, बासी मिठाईले पनि, र चिसो पेयले पनि।

चार चम्चा चिनीको ठाउँमा चार चम्चा सख्खर हाल्नुभयो भने केही बचत भएको छैन।

## अनि साँचो फाइदा कति हो

अब असली कुरा, त्यही आकारमा जति साँचै हो।

सेतो चिनी बनाउने प्रक्रियामा खैरो भाग, अर्थात् मोलासेस, अलग गरिन्छ। रङ्ग, स्वाद र खनिज प्रायः त्यही मोलासेसमा हुन्छन्। सख्खरमा त्यो कहिल्यै अलग गरिँदैन, त्यसैले उखुको रसमा जे थियो, डल्लोमा उही रहन्छ।

खनिजको मात्रा सानो हुन्छ। फलाम, पोटासियम, म्याग्नेसियम र क्याल्सियम केही मात्रामा हुन्छन्, तर यो त्यस्तो खानेकुरा हो जुन चम्चाले खाइन्छ, कचौराले होइन। फलामको लागि सख्खर खाने हो भने त्यति धेरै खानुपर्छ कि त्यो आफैंमा हानिकारक हुन्छ।

दोस्रो फाइदा त्यो हो जुन *हालिँदैन*। परम्परागत तरिकाले बनेको सख्खरमा सल्फर, रासायनिक क्लारिफायर वा कृत्रिम रङ्ग हालिँदैन, जबकि सेतो चिनी बनाउँदा ब्लिचिङ हुन्छ। यो फरक हामी साँच्चै दाबी गर्न सक्छौं।

तेस्रो कुरा स्वाद हो, र यो पोषणको कुरा होइन। सख्खरमा क्यारामेल र दाउराको धुवाँको स्वाद हुन्छ, त्यसैले एक चम्चाले जति काम गर्छ, चिनीको दुई चम्चा चाहिन्थ्यो। कम खाइने भयो भने त्यो बचत हो, तर त्यो बानीको बचत हो, मिठासको होइन।

## जुन फाइदाहरू बढाइचढाइ हुन्

यी दाबीहरू धेरै ठाउँमा पढ्न पाइन्छ, र यिनको पछाडि राम्रो प्रमाण छैन:

- सख्खरले रगत सफा गर्छ
- सख्खरले कलेजो डिटक्स गर्छ
- सख्खरले रक्तअल्पता निको पार्छ
- सख्खरले तौल घटाउँछ

यी कुरा सबैको सख्खरमा लागू हुँदैनन्, हाम्रोमा पनि। सख्खर मिठास हो, औषधि होइन।

आयुर्वेदमा गुडलाई पाचनसँग जोडेर हेरिन्छ, र त्यो परम्परा पुरानो हो। तर परम्परागत मान्यता र प्रमाणित उपचार फरक कुरा हुन्, र हामी दोस्रो भन्न सक्दैनौं।

कसैले "हाम्रो सख्खर स्वास्थ्यकर छ त्यसैले धेरै खान हुन्छ" भन्छ भने त्यो बेच्न लागेको हो। कम खानुहोस्। हाम्रो पनि।

## एक दिनमा कति सख्खर ठीक हो

यसमा सबैभन्दा स्पष्ट मार्गनिर्देशन विश्व स्वास्थ्य सङ्गठनको हो। WHO ले [थपिएको चिनी दैनिक ऊर्जाको १० प्रतिशतभन्दा कम](https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/9789241549028) राख्न सुझाव दिन्छ, र [५ प्रतिशत अर्थात् करिब २५ ग्राम, लगभग ६ चम्चा](https://www.who.int/news/item/04-03-2015-who-calls-on-countries-to-reduce-sugars-intake-among-adults-and-children) भन्दा तल झार्न सके थप फाइदा हुने बताउँछ।

यो सीमाभित्र सख्खर पनि गनिन्छ, चिनी, मह र मिठाई सबैसँगै।

भान्साको भाषामा भन्दा: एक कप चियामा एक देखि डेढ चम्चा सख्खर हुन्छ, करिब ४ देखि ७ ग्राम। बिहान दुई कप र दिउँसो दुई कप चिया पिउनुभयो भने बिस्कुट खानुअघि नै दिनको सीमा प्रायः सकिन्छ।

खाना खाएपछि सानो टुक्रा सख्खर खाने बानी ठीकै हो, यदि बाँकी दिन गुलियो छैन भने।

यो सामान्य मार्गनिर्देशन हो, तपाईंका लागि लेखिएको प्रिस्क्रिप्शन होइन। बालबालिका, कुनै रोग भएका र नियन्त्रित खानपानमा रहेकाहरूले आफ्नै चिकित्सकसँग सोध्नुपर्छ।

## मधुमेह भएकाहरूका लागि

छोटो जवाफ: सख्खर मधुमेहका लागि सुरक्षित विकल्प होइन।

यो चिनी नै हो र रगतको ग्लुकोज बढाउँछ। भाँडो फेरेर समस्या समाधान हुँदैन, र जसले "यो प्राकृतिक हो त्यसैले हुन्छ" भन्छ, उसले तपाईंलाई गलत बाटो देखाइरहेको छ।

यो प्रश्न महत्त्वपूर्ण भएकाले हामीले यसको पूरा जवाफ छुट्टै पृष्ठमा लेखेका छौं। पढ्नुहोस्: [के सख्खर मधुमेहका लागि सुरक्षित छ](/blog/is-jaggery-safe-for-diabetics)। ग्लाइसेमिक इन्डेक्सका सङ्ख्याहरू किन भरपर्दो छैनन् भन्ने पनि त्यहीँ छ।

मधुमेह व्यवस्थापन गर्दै हुनुहुन्छ भने आफ्नो चिकित्सक वा आहार विशेषज्ञको कुरा मान्नुहोस्, कुनै ब्लगको होइन, यो सहित।

## त्यसो भए सख्खर खानु हुन्छ कि हुँदैन

हुन्छ, तर मिठासको रूपमा, औषधिको रूपमा होइन।

दैनिक चिया र परम्परागत खानाका लागि सख्खर छान्नु ठीक हो। यो परिष्कृत छैन, राम्रो डल्लोमा रसायन हालिएको हुँदैन, र उखुमा भएका खनिज अलिकति बाँकी हुन्छन्।

तर स्वास्थ्यको दृष्टिले सबैभन्दा ठूलो सुधार भाँडो फेर्नु होइन, मात्रा घटाउनु हो।

सख्खर र चिनीको पूरा तुलना, स्रोतसहित, [यहाँ छ](/blog/jaggery-vs-sugar), र नेपालीमा छोटो तुलना [यहाँ](/ne/blog/sakhar-ra-chini)। किन्नुअघि साँचो सख्खर कसरी चिन्ने भन्ने कुरा [यहाँ](/ne/blog/sakhar-kasari-chinne) लेखिएको छ।

## बारम्बार सोधिने प्रश्नहरू

### सख्खर खाने फाइदा के के हुन्?

सख्खर परिष्कृत नगरिएको हुनाले फलाम, पोटासियम, म्याग्नेसियम र क्याल्सियम थोरै मात्रामा बाँकी रहन्छन्, र परम्परागत तरिकाले बनेकोमा सल्फर वा रङ्ग हालिँदैन। स्वाद बलियो हुने हुनाले प्रायः कम मात्रामा पुग्छ। तर यी फाइदा सानै छन्।

### सख्खरले रगत सफा गर्छ भन्ने साँचो हो?

होइन। रगत सफा गर्ने, कलेजो डिटक्स गर्ने वा तौल घटाउने दाबीका पछाडि भरपर्दो प्रमाण छैन। यो सबैको सख्खरमा लागू हुन्छ, हाम्रोमा पनि। सख्खर मिठास हो, औषधि होइन।

### दिनमा कति सख्खर खान हुन्छ?

WHO का अनुसार थपिएको चिनी दैनिक ऊर्जाको १० प्रतिशतभन्दा कम, र सकेसम्म करिब २५ ग्राम अर्थात् ६ चम्चाभन्दा तल राख्नुपर्छ। यसमा सख्खर, चिनी, मह र मिठाई सबै गनिन्छन्, छुट्टाछुट्टै होइन।

### मधुमेह भएकाले सख्खर खान हुन्छ?

सुरक्षित विकल्पका रूपमा हुँदैन। सख्खरले पनि रगतको ग्लुकोज बढाउँछ। पूरा जवाफ [यो पृष्ठमा](/blog/is-jaggery-safe-for-diabetics) छ, र निर्णय आफ्नो चिकित्सकसँग सल्लाह गरेर मात्र गर्नुहोस्।

### सख्खर र चिनीमा क्यालोरीको फरक कति हो?

धेरै थोरै। सख्खर पनि प्रायः सुक्रोज नै हो, र वजनको केही भाग पानी र खनिज हुने हुनाले प्रति १०० ग्राम अलि कम पर्छ। चम्चाको हिसाबमा यो फरक तौल वा रगतको चिनीका लागि अर्थपूर्ण छैन।

### बच्चालाई सख्खर दिन हुन्छ?

मिठाईकै रूपमा, थोरै मात्रामा। कृत्रिम रङ्ग हालिएका चकलेटभन्दा सख्खर राम्रो विकल्प हो, तर यो पनि चिनी नै हो र दैनिक सीमाभित्रै गनिन्छ। सानो बच्चालाई कडा टुक्रा नदिनुहोस्, फुटाएर दिनुहोस्।

## अन्तिम कुरा

सख्खरको फाइदा साँचो छ, तर सानो छ। जति ठूलो पारेर लेखिन्छ, त्यति ठूलो होइन।

content:
बिहानको सात बजेको छ, दूध चुल्होमा छ, र हात दुई भाँडाको बीचमा अलमलिएको छ। सख्खर कि चिनी?

यो सानो निर्णय हो, तर दिनहुँ गर्नुपर्छ। सख्खर (sakhar) र चिनी (chini) बीचको फरक के हो भन्ने प्रश्न त्यसैले सबैभन्दा धेरै सोधिन्छ।

हामी सङ्खुवासभाको पहाडमा सख्खर बनाउँछौं। यो लेख छोटो छ र भान्साका लागि हो। पूरा तुलना, स्रोत र सङ्ख्यासहित, अङ्ग्रेजीमा [यहाँ](/blog/jaggery-vs-sugar) छ।

> सख्खर र सेतो चिनीको क्यालोरी लगभग उस्तै हो, र दुवैले रगतको चिनी बढाउँछ। फरक यति हो कि सख्खर परिष्कृत गरिँदैन, त्यसैले फलाम, पोटासियम र म्याग्नेसियम थोरै बाँकी रहन्छ र ब्लिचिङ हुँदैन। दैनिक चिया र परम्परागत खानाका लागि सख्खर राम्रो छनोट हो, तर मात्रा उही सानै राख्नुपर्छ।

खनिज | थोरै मात्रामा फलाम, पोटासियम, म्याग्नेसियम, क्याल्सियम | लगभग शून्य

स्वाद | क्यारामेल र दाउराको धुवाँ, ब्याचअनुसार फरक | तटस्थ, सधैं उही

:::

## भान्सामा वास्तविक फरक के हो

तीन ठाउँमा फरक महसुस हुन्छ।

**चियामा।** सख्खरको स्वाद बलियो हुन्छ, त्यसैले एक चम्चाले चिनीको दुई चम्चाजति काम गर्छ। तर सख्खर सिधै उम्लिरहेको दूधमा हाल्नुभयो भने दूध फुट्छ। यो साँचो समस्या हो र यसको समाधान क्रममा छ, विधिमा होइन। कसरी नफुटाई बनाउने भन्ने पूरा तरिका [यहाँ](/blog/jaggery-tea-without-curdling) छ।

**पकाउँदा।** खीर, हलुवा, सेलरोटी, चाकु र तिलका परिकारमा सख्खर मिल्छ, किनभने यी परिकार सख्खरकै साथमा हुर्केका हुन्।

**बेकिङमा।** यहाँ सख्खर सधैं राम्रो हुँदैन। यसले रङ्ग गाढा बनाउँछ, चाँडो ब्राउन हुन्छ र चिस्यान थप्छ। मेरिङ्ग्यु, सेतो आइसिङ, हल्का केक र सफा सिरपमा सेतो चिनी नै ठीक हो। त्यसका लागि सेतो चिनी प्रयोग गर्नुहोस्, अपराधबोध नगरी।

## चिनीको ठाउँमा सख्खर कसरी हाल्ने

- तौलको हिसाबले एक बराबर एक बाट सुरु गर्नुहोस्, अनि स्वादअनुसार घटाउनुहोस्। धेरैलाई अन्ततः अलि कम पुग्छ।
- चियाका लागि पहिले तातो पानी वा चियामा घोल्नुहोस्, अनि दूध हाल्नुहोस्। [सख्खर धूलो](/products/jaggery-powder) सबैभन्दा छिटो घुल्छ।
- डल्लो प्रयोग गर्दै हुनुहुन्छ भने पहिले कद्दुकसमा रगड्नुहोस्। सिङ्गो टुक्रा तातो दूधमा हाल्नु सबैभन्दा ठूलो गल्ती हो।
- बेकिङमा ओभनको तापक्रम करिब १० डिग्री घटाउनुहोस् र चाँडो जाँच्नुहोस्।

## तर एउटा कुरा सफा गरौं

सख्खर पनि चिनी नै हो।

यो उखुको रस हो जसबाट पानी उडाइएको छ, र बाँकी रहने कुरा प्रायः सुक्रोज हो, त्यही सुक्रोज जुन सेतो प्याकेटमा हुन्छ। यसले रगतको ग्लुकोज बढाउँछ।

त्यसैले "सख्खर स्वास्थ्यकर छ, धेरै खाए पनि हुन्छ" भन्ने कुरा गलत हो। हामी सख्खर बेच्ने मान्छे भएर पनि यही भन्छौं।

मधुमेह भएका मानिसका लागि सख्खर सुरक्षित विकल्प होइन। यसको पूरा जवाफ [यो पृष्ठमा](/blog/is-jaggery-safe-for-diabetics) छ।

WHO ले थपिएको चिनी दैनिक करिब [२५ ग्राम, अर्थात् ६ चम्चाभन्दा तल](https://www.who.int/news/item/04-03-2015-who-calls-on-countries-to-reduce-sugars-intake-among-adults-and-children) राख्न सुझाव दिन्छ। यसमा सख्खर पनि गनिन्छ।

## खैरो चिनी र मह नि?

खैरो चिनीले धेरैलाई अलमल्याउँछ। यो प्रायः सेतो चिनीमै मोलासेस फेरि मिसाएर बनाइन्छ। अर्थात् रङ्ग पछि थपिएको हो, सुरुदेखि बाँकी रहेको होइन। त्यसैले खैरो चिनी सधैं एकनासको खैरो हुन्छ, जबकि साँचो सख्खर कहिल्यै हुँदैन।

मह फरक खानेकुरा हो तर काम उही हो। यो पनि चिनी नै हो र रगतको ग्लुकोज बढाउँछ। एउटा नियम सम्झनुहोस्: एक वर्षभन्दा सानो बच्चालाई मह कहिल्यै नदिनुहोस्।

## बारम्बार सोधिने प्रश्नहरू

### सख्खर र चिनीमा कुन राम्रो?

दैनिक चिया र परम्परागत खानाका लागि सख्खर राम्रो हो, किनभने यो परिष्कृत छैन र यसमा ब्लिचिङ हुँदैन। तर स्वास्थ्यको हिसाबले दुवै चिनी नै हुन्, र सबैभन्दा राम्रो सुधार भनेको दुवैको मात्रा घटाउनु हो।

### सख्खरमा क्यालोरी कम हुन्छ?

नगण्य रूपमा मात्र। सख्खरको केही भाग पानी र खनिज हुने हुनाले प्रति १०० ग्राम अलि कम पर्छ, तर चम्चाको हिसाबमा यो फरक अर्थपूर्ण छैन।

### दिनहुँ चियामा सख्खर हाल्न हुन्छ?

हुन्छ, यदि मात्रा सानो रह्यो भने। एक कपमा एक चम्चा सख्खर WHO को सीमाभित्र पर्छ। दिनमा चार कप गुलियो चिया भने पर्दैन, जुनसुकै मिठास प्रयोग गरे पनि।

### सख्खर हालेको दूध किन फुट्छ?

सख्खरमा भएको अम्ल उम्लिरहेको दूधसँग मिल्दा दूध फुट्छ। समाधान क्रम मिलाउनु हो: पहिले पानी वा चियामा सख्खर घोल्नुहोस्, अनि दूध हाल्नुहोस्, वा भाँडो आगोबाट झारेर मात्र हाल्नुहोस्। पूरा विधि [यहाँ](/blog/jaggery-tea-without-curdling) छ।

### बेकिङमा सख्खर प्रयोग गर्न सकिन्छ?

सकिन्छ, तर सबै ठाउँमा होइन। यसले रङ्ग गाढा बनाउँछ र चाँडो ब्राउन हुन्छ। हल्का केक, मेरिङ्ग्यु र सफा सिरपमा सेतो चिनी नै ठीक हो।

### खैरो चिनी सख्खरजस्तै हो?

होइन। खैरो चिनी प्रायः परिष्कृत सेतो चिनीमा मोलासेस फेरि मिसाएर बनाइन्छ। सख्खर कहिल्यै परिष्कृत गरिँदैन, त्यसैले यसको रङ्ग र खनिज बाँकी रहेका हुन्, फेरि थपिएका होइनन्।

## छोटोमा

चियाका लागि सख्खर छान्नुहोस्। बेकिङका लागि चिनी। स्वास्थ्यका लागि दुवै कम।

content:
पसलमा दुई डल्ला छन्। एउटा चम्किलो, सफा, एकनासको सुनौलो। अर्को गाढा, कतै फुटेको, रङ्ग एकनासको छैन।

धेरैजसो मानिस चम्किलो उठाउँछन्। र प्रायः त्यो नै गलत छनोट हो।

हामी सङ्खुवासभामा सख्खर (sakhar) बनाउँछौं, त्यसैले यो कुरा हामीले धेरै पटक देखेका छौं। यो लेख छोटो छ र पसलमै उभिएको मान्छेका लागि हो। घरमा गरिने सातवटा पूरा परीक्षण अङ्ग्रेजीमा [यहाँ](/blog/how-to-identify-pure-jaggery-sakhar) छ।

> साँचो सख्खर प्रायः गाढा, अलि खस्रो र एकनासको नहुने हुन्छ। चम्किलो, एकदमै सफा र एकनासको सुनौलो डल्लो शङ्कास्पद हुन्छ, किनभने त्यो रङ्ग प्रायः क्लारिफायर वा ब्लिचिङबाट आउँछ। पसलमै हेर्ने चार कुरा हुन्: रङ्ग, कडापन, सतह र स्वाद।

## पहिले बुझ्नुपर्ने कुरा: सख्खरमा के मिसाइन्छ

सस्तो बनाउन र राम्रो देखाउन तीन कुरा गरिन्छ।

- **चिनी मिसाउने।** डल्लोको तौल बढाउन सस्तो चिनी उमालेर मिसाइन्छ।
- **पीठो वा स्टार्च मिसाउने।** तौल बढाउने अर्को सस्तो तरिका।
- **रङ्ग उज्यालो पार्ने।** क्लारिफायर वा ब्लिचिङ एजेन्टले डल्लोलाई चम्किलो सुनौलो बनाइदिन्छ, जुन बिक्रीका लागि राम्रो देखिन्छ।

तेस्रो नै सबैभन्दा सामान्य हो, र त्यही कारण चम्किलो डल्लो शङ्कास्पद हुन्छ।

## पसलमै गर्न सकिने चार जाँच

### १. रङ्ग हेर्नुहोस्

यो सबैभन्दा उपयोगी जाँच हो, र उल्टो लाग्छ।

गाढा खैरो देखि कालो-खैरो रङ्ग सामान्य हो। रङ्ग एकनासको नहुनु, बीचमा हल्का धर्सा हुनु, किनारा फुटेको हुनु, यी सबै साँचो चिन्ह हुन्।

एकदमै चम्किलो, टलक्क टल्केको र सुरुदेखि अन्त्यसम्म एउटै सुनौलो रङ्ग भएको डल्लो शङ्का गर्नुहोस्।

तर एउटा कुरा इमानदारीका साथ भनौं: गाढा हुनु मात्रैले शुद्ध हुन्छ भन्ने होइन। रङ्ग ब्याच, उखु काटेको समय र कति बेर उमालियो भन्नेमा भर पर्छ। रङ्ग पहिलो सङ्केत हो, प्रमाण होइन।

### २. औंलाले थिच्नुहोस्

पहाडी सख्खर राम्ररी उमालिएको हुन्छ, त्यसैले कडा हुन्छ। यो टुक्रिन्छ, पिल्सिँदैन।

औंलाले थिच्दा सजिलै गिज्जिने वा नङ् गाडिने डल्लोमा चिस्यान बढी छ। त्यो आफैंमा मिसावट होइन, तर त्यस्तो डल्लो चाँडै बिग्रन्छ र चाकु बनाउँदा जम्दैन।

### ३. सतह छाम्नुहोस्

औंलाले रगड्नुहोस्।

साँचो सख्खर सुक्खा वा हल्का चिटचिटे हुन्छ। औंलामा सेतो वा खरानी रङ्गको धूलो लाग्यो भने त्यो स्टार्च वा पीठो हुन सक्छ।

अलिकति टुक्रा हातमा मुसार्दा त्यो बालुवाजस्तो किरकिरे लाग्यो भने पनि ध्यान दिनुहोस्।

### ४. एक टुक्रा चाख्नुहोस्

पसलले दिन्छ भने सबैभन्दा भरपर्दो जाँच यही हो।

साँचो सख्खरको स्वाद क्यारामेलजस्तो हुन्छ, अलि धुवाँको स्वाद हुन्छ, र मिठासपछि हल्का खनिजको स्वाद बाँकी रहन्छ।

नुनिलो वा तीतो स्वाद आयो भने त्यो राम्रो चिन्ह होइन। सिधै गुलियो मात्र, अरू केही स्वाद नै नआउने भयो भने त्यसमा चिनी मिसाइएको हुन सक्छ।

## घरमा पुगेपछि गर्ने एउटा जाँच

पसलमा सकिँदैन तर घरमा दुई मिनेटमा हुन्छ।

एक गिलास न्यानो पानीमा सानो टुक्रा सख्खर हाल्नुहोस् र पर्खनुहोस्।

साँचो सख्खर पूरै घुल्छ र पानी सफा गाढा रङ्गको हुन्छ। गिलासको फेदमा सेतो वा खरानी रङ्गको तह बस्यो भने त्यो स्टार्च वा चक हो। माथि केही तैरियो भने त्यो पनि राम्रो चिन्ह होइन।

आयोडिनको थोपा प्रयोग गरेर स्टार्च जाँच्ने तरिका सहित सबै सातवटा परीक्षण [यो पृष्ठमा](/blog/how-to-identify-pure-jaggery-sakhar) विस्तारमा छ।

## एउटा कुरा जुन हामीलाई घाटा हुन्छ

सस्तो डल्लो सधैं नक्कली हुँदैन।

तराईको गुड ठूलो परिमाणमा, समथर जमिनमा, राम्ररी बनाइन्छ। यो सफा स्वादको र एकनासको हुन्छ, र सस्तो हुन्छ। धेरै प्रयोगका लागि यो नै उपयुक्त हो, र हामी त्यो लुकाउँदैनौं।

पहाडी सख्खर र तराईको गुडको फरक के हो भन्ने कुरा [यहाँ](/blog/himalayan-jaggery-sankhuwasabha) लेखिएको छ। मूल्यको फरक किन हुन्छ भन्ने [यहाँ](/sakhar-price)।

फरक भनेको मिसावट होइन। मिसावट अर्कै कुरा हो, र माथिका चार जाँचले त्यही खोज्छ।

प्राविधिक रूपमा सख्खरको बनावट उखुको जात, माटो र बनाउने तरिकाअनुसार फरक पर्छ। यो [गैर-सेन्ट्रिफ्युगल उखु चिनीको अध्ययन](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8314846/) मा उल्लेख छ। अर्थात् एउटा ब्याच अर्कोभन्दा फरक हुनु सामान्य हो, तर सेतो धूलो र किरकिरे स्वाद सामान्य होइन।

## बारम्बार सोधिने प्रश्नहरू

### साँचो सख्खर कसरी चिन्ने?

पसलमै चार कुरा हेर्नुहोस्: रङ्ग गाढा र एकनासको छैन कि छ, औंलाले थिच्दा कडा छ कि गिज्जिन्छ, सतह रगड्दा सेतो धूलो लाग्छ कि लाग्दैन, र स्वादमा क्यारामेल र धुवाँ आउँछ कि सिधै गुलियो मात्र।

### गाढा सख्खर राम्रो कि पहेंलो?

गाढा हुनु सामान्यतया राम्रो सङ्केत हो, तर प्रमाण होइन। रङ्ग उखु काटेको समय र कति बेर उमालियो भन्नेमा भर पर्छ। एकदमै चम्किलो र एकनासको पहेंलो डल्लो भने शङ्कास्पद हुन्छ, किनभने त्यस्तो रङ्ग प्रायः क्लारिफायरबाट आउँछ।

### सख्खर पानीमा पूरै घुल्नुपर्छ?

पर्छ। न्यानो पानीमा साँचो सख्खर पूरै घुल्छ र पानी सफा गाढा रङ्गको हुन्छ। फेदमा सेतो वा खरानी रङ्गको तह बस्यो भने त्यो स्टार्च वा चक हुन सक्छ।

### कडा सख्खर राम्रो कि नरम?

कडा डल्लो राम्ररी उमालिएको र कम चिस्यान भएको सङ्केत हो, र यो लामो समय टिक्छ। नरम डल्लो आफैंमा मिसावट होइन, तर चाँडै बिग्रन्छ र चाकु बनाउँदा जम्दैन।

### सख्खरमा के के मिसाइन्छ?

सामान्यतया तीन कुरा: तौल बढाउन सस्तो चिनी, तौल बढाउन पीठो वा स्टार्च, र रङ्ग उज्यालो बनाउन क्लारिफायर वा ब्लिचिङ एजेन्ट। तेस्रो सबैभन्दा सामान्य हो।

### सस्तो सख्खर नराम्रो हो?

सधैं होइन। तराईको गुड ठूलो परिमाणमा राम्ररी बनाइन्छ र स्वाभाविक रूपमा सस्तो पर्छ। तर धेरै सस्तो डल्लामा चिनी, स्टार्च र क्लारिफायर देखिने सम्भावना बढी हुन्छ, त्यसैले किन्नुअघि जाँच्नुहोस्।

## किन्नुअघि

चम्किलोलाई नपत्याउनुहोस्। गाढा, अलि खस्रो र एकनासको नभएको डल्लो नै प्रायः साँचो हुन्छ।

हाम्रो [सख्खर डल्लो](/products/organic-jaggery-block) र [सख्खर धूलो](/products/jaggery-powder) कसरी बन्छ हेर्न चाहनुहुन्छ भने [यहाँ](/our-story) छ, र सख्खर खाने फाइदाबारे इमानदार कुरा [यहाँ](/ne/blog/sakhar-khane-faida)।

जे किन्नुभयो, सोचेभन्दा कम खानुहोस्।

title: Thekua Recipe for Chhath: How to Make It with Gud
seoTitle: Thekua Recipe for Chhath: How to Make It with Gud (Jaggery)
description: How to make thekua for Chhath with gud or sakhar: the dough, the mould, why it must fry slowly, and how much jaggery to buy for your household.
content:
On the evening of Chhath the ponds and riverbanks of the Terai fill with women standing in the water, facing the setting sun, holding bamboo baskets of fruit and sugarcane. In the middle of every basket, under the bananas, is a pile of thekua (ठेकुवा). In Kathmandu it happens at Kamal Pokhari and along the Bagmati, and the smell of ghee and gud comes off the ghats in the dark.

Chhath is not our festival. We are a hill family who make sakhar (सख्खर) in Sankhuwasabha, and the families who keep Chhath have their own rules for how the offering is made. What we can tell you about is the jaggery, because thekua is made with gud, and gud is what we make. So this is the recipe as it is commonly made, with notes on the ingredient we know best. Where your household does it differently, your household is right.

> Thekua is a hard, sweet biscuit of whole wheat flour, jaggery and ghee, deep fried slowly and offered as prasad at Chhath. You dissolve the gud in a little warm water, rub ghee into the flour, knead a stiff dough with the syrup, press it into a mould and fry it on a low flame until it is brown all the way through.

## Ingredients

- 500 g whole wheat flour (atta)
- 200 g sakhar or gud, grated, or sakhar powder
- 100 ml water
- 75 g ghee for the dough, plus ghee or oil for frying
- 30 g grated dry coconut (optional)
- 1 teaspoon fennel seeds (saunf)
- 4 or 5 green cardamom pods, seeds crushed

This makes about 20 to 25 thekua, depending on how large you shape them.

## Which Gud Is Best for Thekua?

Thekua is one of the few recipes where the jaggery is dissolved first rather than melted, so the form you buy matters less than it does for chaku. A [sakhar block](/products/organic-jaggery-block) grated on the fine side of a grater works well. [Sakhar powder](/products/jaggery-powder) dissolves in warm water in a minute or two without grating, which is a real saving when you are making several batches for the ghat.

Terai gud works just as well as hill sakhar here, and in most Chhath kitchens it is what gets used. The difference you will notice is colour: a darker, wood-fired block gives a darker thekua with a deeper caramel taste. Neither is more correct.

What does matter is that the gud is clean. If you have doubts about a block, our [seven home tests for pure jaggery](/blog/how-to-identify-pure-jaggery-sakhar) take ten minutes, and for an offering it is worth knowing.

## Method

### Step 1: Dissolve the gud

Put the gud and the water in a pan over a low flame and stir until it has completely dissolved. Do not let it boil. You want a syrup, not a caramel.

Strain it through a fine sieve or a clean cloth to catch any cane fibre or grit, then let it cool until it is just warm.

### Step 2: Rub the ghee into the flour

Put the flour in a wide bowl with the fennel, cardamom and coconut. Add the 75 g of ghee and rub it through the flour with your fingertips until the mixture looks like coarse sand.

Test it by squeezing a handful. If it holds its shape, there is enough ghee. If it falls apart, add a spoonful more. This step, the moyan, is what makes thekua crisp and short rather than hard like a stone.

### Step 3: Knead a stiff dough

Pour the warm syrup in a little at a time and knead. You will probably not need all of it at once.

The dough should be stiff, much stiffer than roti dough. A soft dough spreads in the oil and the pattern disappears. Cover it and rest it for 15 minutes.

### Step 4: Shape and press

Take a piece the size of a small lemon, roll it into a ball and flatten it to about a centimetre thick. Press it into a greased wooden thekua mould (sancha) if you have one. If you do not, flatten it in your palm and mark it with the back of a fork or a clean comb.

Shape the whole batch before you start frying, and keep the shaped pieces covered with a cloth so they do not dry and crack.

### Step 5: Fry slowly

Heat the ghee or oil over a medium flame, then turn it down to low before the first batch goes in. Slide the thekua in a few at a time and fry them, turning once or twice, for about 6 to 8 minutes per batch, until they are deep brown on both sides.

This is where most thekua goes wrong. Jaggery browns faster than white sugar. In hot oil the outside turns dark long before the middle is cooked, and you get thekua that are brown on the outside and soft and raw inside. Low and slow is the whole method.

### Step 6: Cool completely

Lift them out onto a rack or a sieve and leave them to cool fully. They come out of the oil slightly soft and harden as they cool, so do not judge the texture until they are cold.

## Why Is Thekua Made for Chhath?

Chhath is a festival of thanks to Surya, the sun, and to Chhathi Maiya. It falls six days after Laxmi Puja in Tihar and runs over four days: the bathing day, the day of kharna, the evening offering to the setting sun and the morning offering to the rising one. Those observing the fast, the vratis, go without water for long stretches of it.

Thekua is at the centre of the prasad carried to the water in the bamboo soop and daura, with fruit, sugarcane and coconut. It is made from things a household has in the season: new wheat, gud and ghee. It keeps for days without spoiling, which matters for an offering carried to the ghat and shared afterwards.

In many households the prasad is made with particular care. The kitchen is cleaned, the utensils are kept apart, and nobody tastes anything before it is offered. Some families still cook it on a clay chulha. We mention this so that anyone making thekua for the first time for a Chhath household knows to ask how that household does it.

## How Much Gud Do You Need for Chhath?

The recipe above uses 200 g of gud for 500 g of flour. Scale from there.

:::table How much gud to buy for thekua
Flour | Gud or sakhar | Roughly how many thekua
500 g | 200 g | 20 to 25
1 kg | 400 g | 40 to 50
2 kg | 800 g | 80 to 100
:::

A household making thekua for its own soop and for sharing with neighbours is usually somewhere in the middle of that table. One 1kg block covers two kilos of flour, with some to spare for the kharna kheer. If you will be making [chaku for Maghe Sankranti](/blog/chaku-recipe-maghe-sankranti) in January too, the same block does both.

Buy it a week or two early. Chhath falls on the same day for everyone who keeps it, and the week before is when every shop in the Terai runs short.

## How to Store Thekua

In an airtight tin at room temperature, once they are completely cold. Kept dry, thekua last about two weeks. If they soften, the tin was not airtight or they went in warm.

Do not refrigerate them. Condensation softens the crust and they go stale faster in a fridge than in a cupboard.

## The Honest Note About Eating It

Thekua is flour, gud and ghee, fried. It is a festival food and it should be eaten like one.

Making it with jaggery rather than white sugar does not make it a health food. Jaggery is [non-centrifugal cane sugar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-centrifugal_cane_sugar), and the small amounts of minerals it carries do not change what it is. We have set out the whole comparison in [sakhar and sugar, honestly](/blog/jaggery-vs-sugar). The [WHO advice on free sugars](https://www.who.int/news/item/04-03-2015-who-calls-on-countries-to-reduce-sugars-intake-among-adults-and-children) applies to gud exactly as it applies to chini. If someone in the family has diabetes, please read [whether jaggery is safe for diabetics](/blog/is-jaggery-safe-for-diabetics) before the prasad goes round.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### What is thekua made of?

Whole wheat flour, gud or jaggery, and ghee, usually flavoured with fennel, cardamom and dry coconut. The gud is dissolved in a little water and kneaded into the flour, and the biscuits are pressed into a mould and deep fried slowly.

### Can I make thekua with sugar instead of gud?

You can, and some households do. It gives a paler, sweeter biscuit without the caramel depth. Gud is the traditional choice for Chhath, and most families keep to it for the offering.

### Why are my thekua raw inside?

The oil was too hot. Jaggery browns quickly, so the outside darkens before the centre cooks. Fry on a low flame for 6 to 8 minutes per batch, and make them no more than a centimetre thick.

### Why did my thekua turn out too hard?

Usually too little ghee in the dough, or too much syrup making a dense dough. Rub in enough ghee that a squeezed handful of flour holds its shape. They also harden as they cool, so a thekua that seems right when hot will be crisper cold.

### How long does thekua last?

About two weeks in an airtight tin at room temperature. Keep them dry and out of the fridge.

### How much gud do I need for thekua?

About 200 g of gud for every 500 g of flour, which makes 20 to 25 thekua. A 1kg block covers two kilos of flour.

### Is thekua healthy?

It is a fried festival sweet made with flour, jaggery and ghee. Using jaggery instead of white sugar does not make it a health food. Eat it at Chhath and share it, which is what it is for.

## One Last Thing

If you are making thekua for the first time, make a small batch a few days before Chhath to learn how your flame behaves. The heat is the part nobody gets right from reading.

title: Sel Roti with Sakhar: A Jaggery Sel Roti Recipe for Tihar
seoTitle: Sel Roti Recipe with Sakhar (Jaggery) for Tihar
description: How to make sel roti with sakhar instead of sugar for Tihar: the batter, why jaggery needs cooler oil, and how much to buy. Honest about the trade-off.
content:
The rice goes into the water the night before. By morning somebody is at the grinder, somebody is heating a deep pan of oil, and the first ring of batter goes in with a hiss that tells the whole house Tihar has started. Sel roti (सेल रोटी) is made in the same way in hill kitchens across Nepal, and every family is sure theirs is the right one.

We should say at the start that most sel roti is made with white sugar, and that is the recipe most families use. Making it with sakhar (सख्खर), our jaggery, is a variation, not the original. It gives a darker, deeper-tasting roti that some people love and some find too heavy. This recipe is for anyone who wants to try it, and it is honest about where jaggery makes the job harder.

> Sel roti with sakhar is the Tihar ring bread made with jaggery in place of white sugar. Soak rice overnight, grind it with sakhar powder, ghee and a little banana into a thick batter, rest it, and pour it in a ring into hot oil. Jaggery browns faster than sugar, so the oil needs to be a little cooler.

## Ingredients

- 500 g rice, soaked in water for at least 6 hours or overnight
- 150 g sakhar powder
- 75 g ghee, melted
- 1 small ripe banana (optional)
- 150 to 200 ml water or milk, as needed
- Oil or ghee for deep frying

This makes about 15 to 20 sel roti, depending on the size of the ring.

## Which Jaggery Works for Sel Roti?

Use [sakhar powder](/products/jaggery-powder). It grinds into the batter evenly with the rice and does not leave lumps. A [sakhar block](/products/organic-jaggery-block) will work if you grate it finely first, but lumps of jaggery in the batter burn in the oil and leave dark spots on the roti.

A darker, wood-fired sakhar makes a darker sel roti. If you want something closer to the colour of the sugar version, use a little less sakhar and make up the sweetness with a spoonful of sugar. We would rather tell you that than pretend jaggery gives the same result.

## Method

### Step 1: Soak and drain the rice

Soak the rice in plenty of water for at least 6 hours, or overnight. Drain it well in a sieve.

Any rice that is not sticky works. Many families use the ordinary rice they eat every day.

### Step 2: Grind the batter

Grind the soaked rice with the sakhar powder, the banana if you are using it, and a little of the water or milk. Add the liquid a few spoonfuls at a time.

The batter should be slightly grainy, not completely smooth, and thick enough that it pours from a spoon in a steady ribbon. Too thin and the ring breaks up in the oil. Too thick and it will not pour.

### Step 3: Add the ghee and rest

Stir in the melted ghee and leave the batter to rest for about 30 minutes, covered. Stir it again before you start frying, because the rice settles.

### Step 4: Heat the oil, then lower it

Heat the oil in a deep pan over a medium flame. Test it with a drop of batter: it should sink slightly, then rise steadily to the surface with bubbles around it. If it rises instantly and browns in seconds, the oil is too hot for a jaggery batter.

Sel roti made with sugar is usually fried in hotter oil than this. With sakhar, keep it at medium or a little below.

### Step 5: Pour the ring

Take a handful of batter and pour it into the oil in a circle, letting it stream from the side of your hand or through a cone of cloth or a plastic bottle. Close the ring where you started.

Your first few will not be round. Nobody's are.

### Step 6: Fry and turn

When the underside has set and turned golden, turn the roti with a thin stick or a pair of chopsticks and fry the other side. Each side takes about a minute or two.

Watch the colour closely. Jaggery takes a sel roti from golden to dark brown much faster than sugar does. Lift it out when it is a shade lighter than you want, because it keeps darkening for a moment out of the oil.

Drain the roti standing upright on a stick or in a sieve, so the oil runs off and the ring keeps its shape.

## Why Is Sel Roti Made for Tihar?

Tihar is the five-day festival of lights, and sel roti is one of the foods most families make for it, especially for Bhai Tika, when sisters give tika to their brothers and a plate of sweets and sel roti is set out. It is also made for Dashain, for weddings, and for any day that calls for a celebration.

It is fried in quantity because it keeps for several days and travels well. Many families pack it for relatives who could not come home.

## How Much Sakhar Do You Need for Tihar?

The recipe above uses 150 g of sakhar powder for 500 g of rice. Scale from there.

:::table How much sakhar to buy for sel roti
Rice | Sakhar powder | Roughly how many sel roti
500 g | 150 g | 15 to 20
1 kg | 300 g | 30 to 40
2 kg | 600 g | 60 to 80
:::

A 250g pouch of powder covers one and a half kilos of rice. For a household making a big batch for Bhai Tika and for sending to relatives, three pouches is usually enough. If you only want to try the jaggery version once, one pouch and a small batch is the sensible way to find out whether your family likes it. For [chaku at Maghe Sankranti](/blog/chaku-recipe-maghe-sankranti), which melts the jaggery rather than grinding it, the block is the better buy.

## How to Store Sel Roti

At room temperature in a covered container, once completely cool. Sel roti keeps for several days this way, and firms up as it sits.

Warm it through on a dry pan or tawa before eating. A roti made with sakhar tends to soften a little faster in humid weather than one made with sugar, because jaggery draws moisture from the air. Our [storage guide](/blog/how-to-store-jaggery-sakhar) explains why.

## The Honest Note About Eating It

Sel roti is rice, sugar and fat, fried. Making it with jaggery does not change that in any way that matters to your health. Jaggery is [non-centrifugal cane sugar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-centrifugal_cane_sugar): a sugar with some of the cane left in, not a different food. The [WHO guideline on sugars](https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/9789241549028) counts it the same as white sugar, and so should you.

Make it with sakhar because you like the taste. If you want the full comparison, it is in [sakhar and sugar, honestly](/blog/jaggery-vs-sugar).

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Can you make sel roti with jaggery?

Yes. Use sakhar powder in place of sugar, at about 150 g for every 500 g of rice. The roti comes out darker with a deeper, caramel taste. Fry it in slightly cooler oil, because jaggery browns faster than sugar.

### Is sel roti traditionally made with sugar or jaggery?

Most families make it with white sugar today. Jaggery sel roti is a variation that some households prefer.

### Why is my sel roti dark outside and raw inside?

The oil is too hot, and with jaggery that happens sooner than with sugar. Lower the flame, test with a drop of batter, and lift each roti out when it is a shade lighter than you want.

### Why does my sel roti break in the oil?

The batter is too thin, or it was not stirred before frying and the rice had settled. Add a spoonful of rice flour or grind in a little more soaked rice to thicken it.

### How long should rice be soaked for sel roti?

At least 6 hours, and overnight is easier. Rice that has not soaked long enough grinds into a gritty batter that will not hold a ring.

### How long does sel roti last?

Several days at room temperature in a covered container. Warm it on a dry pan before eating.

### Can I use a sakhar block instead of powder?

You can, if you grate it very finely first. Lumps of jaggery in the batter burn in the oil and leave dark spots, which is why powder is easier.

## One Last Thing

If this is your first jaggery sel roti, make a half batch the week before Tihar and see what your family thinks. Some people will not go back. Some will ask you to make the usual kind next year, and that is a fair answer too.

title: Yomari Recipe: Chaku Filling for Yomari Punhi
seoTitle: Yomari Recipe with Chaku Filling for Yomari Punhi
description: How to make yomari for Yomari Punhi: rice flour dough, a chaku and til filling you can make from sakhar, shaping the tail, and how long to steam them.
content:
Break a yomari (योमरी) open while it is still hot and the filling runs. It is dark, glossy and sticky, chaku and sesame melted inside a shell of steamed rice flour, and it burns your fingers every single time. Newar families in the Kathmandu Valley make yomari at the full moon of Thinla, in December, when the rice harvest is in.

Yomari Punhi is not our festival, and we are not Newar. We make the sakhar (सख्खर) that chaku is made from, in the hills of Sankhuwasabha. So this recipe is written by people who know the filling well and the tradition only from the outside. The families who have made yomari for generations will do it better than any page can explain. This is for everyone else who wants to try.

> Yomari is a Newar steamed dumpling of rice flour, shaped like a fig with a pointed tail and filled with chaku and sesame, made for Yomari Punhi in December. You knead rice flour with boiling water, shape a hollow cone, fill it with soft chaku mixed with roasted til, seal it into a tail and steam it for about 15 minutes.

## Ingredients

For the dough:

- 500 g fine rice flour
- About 350 ml boiling water

For the filling:

- 250 g chaku, or 250 g sakhar block and 1 tablespoon ghee to make it
- 50 g white sesame seeds (til), roasted
- Ghee for your hands

This makes about 12 to 15 yomari.

## Chaku or Sakhar for the Filling?

The traditional filling is chaku (चाकु): jaggery cooked with ghee and worked until it thickens. If you can buy chaku made in Tokha, use it. Melt it gently with a spoon of water and stir in the roasted sesame.

If you cannot, you can make a soft filling from a [sakhar block](/products/organic-jaggery-block). This is simpler than making chaku to eat on its own, because a yomari filling needs to stay soft and runny when steamed, not set hard.

We do not sell chaku. We sell the jaggery it is made from, and for a filling that is all you need. If you want to make proper chaku for Maghe Sankranti as well, the full method is in our [chaku recipe](/blog/chaku-recipe-maghe-sankranti).

## Method

### Step 1: Make the filling

If you are using chaku, melt it over a low flame with a tablespoon of water, stir in the roasted sesame and let it cool until it is thick enough to hold on a spoon.

If you are starting from sakhar, break the block into small pieces and melt it with the ghee and 2 tablespoons of water over a low flame, stirring until smooth. Let it simmer for 3 to 5 minutes until it thickens slightly. Do not take it to the thread stage you would use for chaku, or the filling will set hard inside the yomari. Stir in the sesame and let it cool until it is thick and sticky.

### Step 2: Make the dough

Put the rice flour in a bowl and pour in the boiling water a little at a time, stirring with a spoon. When it is cool enough to touch, knead it with greased hands into a smooth, soft dough.

Rice flour has no gluten, so the dough will not stretch. It should be soft enough to press without cracking. If it cracks, add a spoonful of hot water and knead again. Keep it covered with a damp cloth the whole time, because it dries out quickly.

### Step 3: Shape the cone

Take a piece of dough the size of a lime and roll it into a ball. Press your thumb into it and work it round into a deep cup with thin walls, then pinch the top into a narrow cone, like the neck of a bottle.

This is the hard part, and your first few will be thick and uneven. That is normal.

### Step 4: Fill and seal

Spoon the filling into the cone until it is about two-thirds full. Pinch the opening closed and draw it out into a pointed tail. The finished shape is a plump fig, or a fish, with a tail at one end.

Make sure there are no cracks. Filling that leaks in the steamer burns onto the pan.

### Step 5: Steam

Set the yomari on a greased plate or a leaf in a steamer over boiling water, with space between them. Cover and steam for about 15 minutes, until the dough looks slightly translucent and no longer chalky.

### Step 6: Eat them warm

Let them cool for a minute or two before you bite into one. The filling stays very hot for longer than the dough does.

## What Is Yomari Punhi?

Yomari Punhi is the Newar festival held on the full moon of Thinla, which falls in December. It comes after the rice harvest, and yomari are made from the new rice. The name is usually explained as "tasty bread" in Nepal Bhasa.

Families offer yomari at home before eating them, and children go from house to house singing songs and asking for yomari, much as children go out singing at Tihar. The festival is part of Kathmandu Valley life in a way that nothing in our own hill calendar quite matches.

If you want to see it done properly, visit a Newar household or a Valley neighbourhood that makes yomari that evening. It will teach you more than this page can.

## How Much Sakhar Do You Need for Yomari?

For a filling made from sakhar, the recipe above uses 250 g for 12 to 15 yomari.

:::table How much sakhar to buy for yomari
Rice flour | Sakhar for filling | Roughly how many yomari
500 g | 250 g | 12 to 15
1 kg | 500 g | 25 to 30
2 kg | 1 kg | 50 to 60
:::

One 1kg block fills 50 to 60 yomari, which is a large family gathering. Yomari Punhi comes about a month before Maghe Sankranti, so if you are making chaku in January as well, one block can often cover both.

## How to Store Yomari

Yomari are best eaten the day they are made. Kept covered at room temperature, they last a day or two, and the dough firms up.

To reheat, steam them again for a few minutes. Some people fry day-old yomari in a little ghee, which is very good. Do not microwave them dry, because the filling boils and bursts through the dough.

## The Honest Note About Eating It

Yomari is rice flour, jaggery and sesame. It is a festival food and very sweet in the middle.

The jaggery in the filling is still sugar. Unrefined [non-centrifugal cane sugar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-centrifugal_cane_sugar) carries a little more of the cane than white sugar, but not enough to make yomari a health food. The [WHO advice on free sugars](https://www.who.int/news/item/04-03-2015-who-calls-on-countries-to-reduce-sugars-intake-among-adults-and-children) applies to it in full. If diabetes is a question in your family, please read [whether jaggery is safe for diabetics](/blog/is-jaggery-safe-for-diabetics) first.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### What is the filling in yomari?

The traditional sweet filling is chaku, which is jaggery cooked with ghee, mixed with roasted sesame. Some families also make yomari filled with khuwa, sweetened milk solids.

### Can I make yomari filling from jaggery instead of chaku?

Yes. Melt a sakhar block with a little ghee and water, simmer it for a few minutes until it thickens slightly, and stir in roasted sesame. Do not cook it as far as you would for chaku, or it will set hard inside the yomari.

### Why does my yomari dough crack?

It is too dry, or it has been left uncovered. Knead in a spoonful of hot water, and keep the dough under a damp cloth while you shape.

### Why did the filling leak out when steaming?

The tail was not sealed properly, or the walls of the cone were too thin. Pinch the opening firmly closed and fill the cone only two-thirds full.

### How long should yomari be steamed?

About 15 minutes, until the dough turns slightly translucent. Undercooked dough tastes chalky.

### When is Yomari Punhi?

On the full moon of Thinla in the Nepal Sambat calendar, which falls in December.

### How much jaggery do I need for yomari?

About 250 g of sakhar for 500 g of rice flour, which makes 12 to 15 yomari.

## One Last Thing

Shaping yomari is a skill that takes more than one evening. Make a few, laugh at them, eat them anyway, and the next batch will be better.

If you want to know where the jaggery in your filling comes from, [this is the story](/our-story), and the [tradition of chaku making in Tokha](https://www.newsonair.gov.in/kathmandu-streets-full-oof-fragrance-of-freshly-cookled-jaggery-for-maghe-sankranti) is worth reading about too.

title: How to Eat Sakhar: Everyday Ways Nepal Uses Jaggery
seoTitle: How to Eat Jaggery (Sakhar): Everyday Ways Nepal Uses It
description: How to eat jaggery the way Nepal does: a piece after dal bhat, in chiya, with dahi and chiura, in roti with ghee and in festival sweets. And how much.
content:
After dal bhat in a hill house, somebody reaches up to a shelf, breaks a corner off a dark block and passes the pieces round. Nobody calls it dessert. It is just what happens after a meal, the way chiya happens in the morning.

That is the oldest way to eat sakhar (सख्खर), or jaggery, and it is still the simplest. But most people who buy a block for the first time are really asking something else: what do I actually do with it? Here is how Nepal uses it, from the everyday to the festival, with what we have learned about each.

> The simplest way to eat jaggery is a small piece after a meal, the way hill households in Nepal always have. Beyond that, use sakhar wherever you would use sugar: in chiya, with dahi and chiura, melted into ghee for roti, or cooked into sweets like chaku, thekua and sel roti. Use less than you think you need.

## How Do Nepalis Eat Sakhar Every Day?

### A piece after a meal

Break off a piece about the size of a fingertip and eat it after dal bhat. In the hills this is the most common way sakhar is eaten, and it needs no recipe at all.

It works best with a hard, well-reduced [sakhar block](/products/organic-jaggery-block), which breaks into clean pieces instead of crumbling or bending.

### In chiya

Sakhar chiya is the second most common use, and the one that goes wrong most often, because jaggery can curdle hot milk. The fix is in the order you add things, and we have written the whole method in [how to make jaggery tea without curdling the milk](/blog/jaggery-tea-without-curdling).

For tea, the [powder](/products/jaggery-powder) is easier. It measures like sugar and dissolves without leaving grit.

### With dahi and chiura

A spoon of sakhar powder or a few grated shavings over dahi, or dahi and chiura, is a quick sweet breakfast. In the Terai, dahi-chiura with gud is part of Maghe Sankranti. The jaggery gives the curd a darker, caramel taste that white sugar does not.

Add it just before you eat. Stirred into dahi and left for an hour, jaggery draws water out of the curd and turns it thin.

### With roti and ghee

Warm roti with a little ghee and crumbled sakhar rolled inside is one of the simplest sweets there is, and one a lot of Nepali children grow up on. Melt the sakhar into the warm ghee first if you want it to spread.

### With dhido

Some hill households eat dhido with ghee and a little sakhar, especially buckwheat or millet dhido on a cold morning. It is not how most people eat dhido, and it is not a meal we would pretend is common. But if you grew up with it, you already know it works.

### In milk at night

Warm milk with sakhar is a common bedtime drink. It can curdle for the same reason chiya can: take the milk off the heat and let it cool a little before you stir the sakhar in.

## How Do You Cook With Sakhar?

### In place of sugar

Jaggery can replace white sugar in most recipes, weight for weight, with three differences worth knowing.

- It is less sweet and more caramel, so some people add a little more. Taste before you do.
- It carries a little more moisture, so baked things come out softer and darker.
- It browns and burns faster, so fried and baked things need a lower heat.

For the full comparison of the two forms, [jaggery powder vs block](/blog/jaggery-powder-vs-block) goes through which suits which job.

### In achar and tarkari

A small piece of sakhar rounds off sour tomato achar, lapsi achar or a sharp tarkari, much as a pinch of sugar would. Use very little. The aim is balance, not sweetness.

### In festival sweets

This is where jaggery is not a substitute but the point.

- [Chaku](/blog/chaku-recipe-maghe-sankranti) for Maghe Sankranti, made by working melted sakhar with ghee and sesame.
- [Thekua](/blog/thekua-recipe-chhath) for Chhath, made with gud, flour and ghee.
- [Yomari](/blog/yomari-chaku-recipe) for Yomari Punhi, filled with chaku and sesame.
- [Sel roti with sakhar](/blog/sel-roti-sakhar) for Tihar, a darker variation on the sugar version.

## How Much Sakhar Should You Eat?

Less than you think. We make it for a living, and we would still say that.

Sakhar is sugar. It is [non-centrifugal cane sugar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-centrifugal_cane_sugar), which means some of the cane is left in, but not enough to change what it does in your body. The [WHO guideline on sugars](https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/9789241549028) counts it as a free sugar, the same as white sugar. [The WHO suggests](https://www.who.int/news/item/04-03-2015-who-calls-on-countries-to-reduce-sugars-intake-among-adults-and-children) that adults keep free sugars below 10% of their daily energy, and ideally below 5%, which is about 25 g a day.

A piece after a meal and a spoon in your chiya is already most of that. We have gone through the claims people make about jaggery, one at a time, in [what jaggery does and does not do](/blog/jaggery-health-claims-truth). If you have diabetes, please read [whether jaggery is safe for diabetics](/blog/is-jaggery-safe-for-diabetics) before adding any.

## How Do You Keep Sakhar Once It Is Open?

In an airtight container, away from steam and damp. Sakhar pulls moisture out of the air and goes sticky in the monsoon. A block lasts much longer than powder once opened. Our [storage guide](/blog/how-to-store-jaggery-sakhar) covers what to do when it has already gone soft.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### How do you eat jaggery?

The simplest way is a small piece after a meal. You can also use it in chiya, with dahi and chiura, rolled into roti with ghee, or anywhere you would use sugar in cooking. In Nepal it is also the base of festival sweets like chaku, thekua and yomari.

### Can I eat jaggery directly?

Yes. A small piece eaten on its own after a meal is the most traditional way to eat sakhar in the hills of Nepal. A hard block breaks into clean pieces for this.

### Can jaggery replace sugar in cooking?

In most recipes, yes, weight for weight. It is less sweet and more caramel in taste, it makes baked things softer and darker, and it burns faster, so cook on a lower heat.

### Can I mix jaggery with curd?

Yes. Add it just before you eat. If jaggery is stirred into dahi and left to stand, it draws water from the curd and makes it thin.

### Why does jaggery curdle milk?

Jaggery is slightly acidic, and hot milk proteins clump when acid meets them at high heat. Let the milk cool a little before adding jaggery. The full method is in our jaggery tea guide.

### How much jaggery can I eat in a day?

The WHO counts jaggery as a free sugar, the same as white sugar, and suggests adults keep free sugars below 10% of daily energy, ideally below 5%, which is about 25 g. A small piece and a spoon in your tea already come close to that.

### What is the best time to eat jaggery?

There is no good evidence that timing matters. Traditionally it is eaten after a meal, and that is as good a time as any. The amount matters much more than the hour.

## One Last Thing

If you are new to sakhar, start with a piece after dinner and a spoon in your morning chiya. That will tell you more about whether you like it than any recipe.

title: Sakhar Kheer: How to Make Jaggery Kheer Without Curdling
seoTitle: Jaggery Kheer Recipe: Sakhar Kheer That Does Not Curdle
description: How to make kheer with jaggery (sakhar) without the milk splitting: the one step that matters, how much to use, and what to do if it has curdled.
content:
The milk has been reducing for forty minutes, the rice has gone soft and the whole kitchen smells of cardamom. Then the jaggery goes in, the pot turns grainy in seconds, and forty minutes of work is a pan of sweet curds. Almost everyone who makes kheer with sakhar (सख्खर) for the first time loses one pot this way.

It is avoidable, and the fix is one step in the method. Kheer (खीर) made with jaggery tastes deeper and darker than the white-sugar version, with a caramel note that suits the rice and cardamom well. The only thing it asks is that you add the jaggery at the right moment.

> To make jaggery kheer without curdling, cook the rice in milk until soft and thick, take the pan off the heat, let it stand for three to five minutes, and only then stir in the sakhar a little at a time. Jaggery is slightly acidic, and acid added to milk at the boil splits it.

## Ingredients

- 1 litre full-fat milk
- 60 g rice, washed and soaked for 30 minutes
- 100 g sakhar powder, or a sakhar block grated finely
- 1 tablespoon ghee
- 4 green cardamom pods, seeds crushed
- 1 tablespoon cashews and 1 tablespoon raisins (optional)

This makes 4 to 5 bowls.

## Which Jaggery Is Best for Kheer?

[Sakhar powder](/products/jaggery-powder) is the easiest, because it dissolves quickly in warm milk without lumps. A [sakhar block](/products/organic-jaggery-block) works if you grate it finely first, and it is cheaper by weight if you make kheer often.

A darker, wood-fired sakhar gives a darker, tan kheer. If you are used to white kheer, the colour is the first surprise. It is not a mistake.

The kheer in the photograph above is made with khejur gur, the date palm jaggery Bengal makes in winter. That is a different product from cane sakhar, boiled from palm sap, and we do not make it. It gives a lighter colour and a different, more floral taste. Cane sakhar gives a heavier caramel one. Both make good kheer.

## Method

### Step 1: Soak the rice

Wash the rice and soak it in water for 30 minutes. Drain it. Soaked rice cooks evenly and releases its starch into the milk, which is what thickens kheer.

### Step 2: Fry the rice in ghee

Warm the ghee in a heavy pan and fry the drained rice for a minute or two, stirring, until it smells nutty. Many Nepali kitchens do this, and it keeps the grains from turning to mush.

### Step 3: Simmer in milk

Pour in the milk, bring it to the boil, then turn the flame low. Let it simmer for 35 to 45 minutes, stirring often and scraping the bottom so nothing catches.

It is ready when the rice is completely soft and the milk has reduced by about a third and coats the back of a spoon.

### Step 4: Add cardamom and nuts

Stir in the crushed cardamom, and the cashews and raisins if you are using them. Simmer for two more minutes.

### Step 5: Take it off the heat, then add the sakhar

This is the step that matters. Turn off the flame and move the pan off the burner. Let it stand for three to five minutes, so the milk is hot but no longer at the boil.

Now stir in the sakhar a spoonful at a time, letting each dissolve before adding the next. Taste as you go. You may want less than 100 g.

If you want to be completely safe, dissolve the sakhar in two tablespoons of warm water first, strain it, and stir the syrup in instead. It takes a minute longer and removes the risk entirely.

The reason is the same one that splits jaggery tea, and we have explained it in full in [how to make jaggery tea without curdling the milk](/blog/jaggery-tea-without-curdling).

### Step 6: Serve warm or cold

Serve it warm, or chill it. Kheer thickens a lot as it cools, so if you are serving it cold, stop cooking it a little thinner than you want. Do not put it back on the heat once the sakhar is in.

## What If Your Kheer Has Already Curdled?

It is still safe to eat. It is just grainy.

You can rescue some of the texture by blending it briefly, which turns it into something closer to a smooth pudding. Or strain off the thin whey and eat the rest as it is. Next time, wait longer before the sakhar goes in.

## When Is Kheer Made in Nepal?

On Saun 15, Kheer Khane Din, when households across Nepal make kheer in the middle of the monsoon planting season.

At Chhath, the kharna prasad in many households is kheer sweetened with gud, eaten after the day's fast. If you are making [thekua for Chhath](/blog/thekua-recipe-chhath), the same jaggery covers both.

And for any pasni, puja or birthday that calls for something sweet, kheer is often the first thing made.

## How Much Sakhar Do You Need for Kheer?

About 100 g for every litre of milk, which makes 4 to 5 bowls. A 250g pouch of powder covers two to three pots. A 1kg block covers about ten.

## The Honest Note About Eating It

Kheer made with jaggery is still a sweet made with sugar. Sakhar is [non-centrifugal cane sugar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-centrifugal_cane_sugar), and the [WHO guideline on sugars](https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/9789241549028) treats it the same as white sugar. One bowl of this kheer carries around 20 g of sakhar, which is most of the [roughly 25 g a day the WHO suggests](https://www.who.int/news/item/04-03-2015-who-calls-on-countries-to-reduce-sugars-intake-among-adults-and-children) as an ideal limit for an adult. Make it for the day it is for. If diabetes is in the family, please read [whether jaggery is safe for diabetics](/blog/is-jaggery-safe-for-diabetics) first.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Why does kheer curdle when jaggery is added?

Jaggery is slightly acidic, and milk proteins clump when acid meets them at boiling temperature. Take the kheer off the heat and let it stand for three to five minutes before adding the jaggery.

### Can I add jaggery while the kheer is cooking?

It is better not to. Adding jaggery to boiling milk is the most common reason jaggery kheer splits. Cook the rice and milk first, then add the jaggery off the heat.

### How much jaggery should I use in kheer?

About 100 g for a litre of milk, added a spoonful at a time. Taste as you go, because jaggery is less sweet than sugar in some batches and sweeter in others.

### Is jaggery powder or block better for kheer?

Powder, because it dissolves quickly and evenly. A block works if you grate it finely first.

### Can I make kheer with date palm jaggery?

Yes. Khejur gur, the date palm jaggery of Bengal, makes a well-known kheer. It is a different product from cane sakhar, lighter and more floral in taste.

### Is curdled kheer safe to eat?

Yes. It is grainy but safe. Blend it briefly for a smoother texture, or eat it as it is.

### How long does kheer keep?

About two days in the fridge, covered. Stir it before serving, because it thickens as it stands.

## One Last Thing

Every cook who makes jaggery kheer loses one pot. If you wait those three minutes before the sakhar goes in, it does not have to be yours.
